Question

For each diagram below, a circle is sliced into congruent sectors. An angle, which subtends an integer count of the sectors, is indicated by an circular arc near the center of the circle. You will determine the measure of the angle using degrees, radians, and (fractions of) turns. All radian measures will be expressed in exact form, as a fraction of \(\pi\). All fractions will be shown in reduced form, using improper fractions instead of mixed numbers.

Unlike temperature, where Fahrenheit and Celsius disagree on 0, all three units of angle measure agree on 0. All three measures grow linearly with arc length of a unit circle, so conversions are simple proportions, and the conversion factors can be expressed with the following equivalences.

\[360^{\circ}~=~2\pi \text{ radians}~=~1\text{ turn}\]

Express the following angles using degrees, radians, and turns.

Circle 1

  • The circle below is cut into 8 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\theta\) (theta), subtends 1 of the sectors.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER1## degrees.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER2##\(\pi\bigg/\)##ANSWER3## radians.

  • As a decimal approximation, the angle is ##ANSWER4## radians.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER5##\(\bigg/\)##ANSWER6## turns.

  • As a decimal, the angle is ##ANSWER7## turns.

Circle 2

  • The circle below is cut into 6 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\phi\) (phi), subtends 5 of the sectors.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER8## degrees.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER9##\(\pi\bigg/\)##ANSWER10## radians.

  • As a decimal approximation, the angle is ##ANSWER11## radians.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER12##\(\bigg/\)##ANSWER13## turns.

  • As a decimal, the angle is ##ANSWER14## turns.

Circle 3

  • The circle below is cut into 4 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\omega\) (omega), subtends 1 of the sectors.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER15## degrees.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER16##\(\pi\bigg/\)##ANSWER17## radians.

  • As a decimal approximation, the angle is ##ANSWER18## radians.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER19##\(\bigg/\)##ANSWER20## turns.

  • As a decimal, the angle is ##ANSWER21## turns.

Circle 4

  • The circle below is cut into 18 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\psi\) (psi), subtends 6 of the sectors.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER22## degrees.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER23##\(\pi\bigg/\)##ANSWER24## radians.

  • As a decimal approximation, the angle is ##ANSWER25## radians.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER26##\(\bigg/\)##ANSWER27## turns.

  • As a decimal, the angle is ##ANSWER28## turns.

Circle 5

  • The circle below is cut into 20 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\beta\) (beta), subtends 16 of the sectors.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER29## degrees.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER30##\(\pi\bigg/\)##ANSWER31## radians.

  • As a decimal approximation, the angle is ##ANSWER32## radians.

  • The angle is ##ANSWER33##\(\bigg/\)##ANSWER34## turns.

  • As a decimal, the angle is ##ANSWER35## turns.

Solution

Circle 1

  • The circle is cut into 8 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\theta\) (theta), subtends 1 of the sectors.

The angle is \(45^{\circ}\), which is \(\frac{1}{4}\pi\) radians, approximately 0.785398163397448 radians, which is \(\frac{1}{8}\) of a turn, which is 0.125 turns.

Circle 2

  • The circle is cut into 6 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\phi\) (phi), subtends 5 of the sectors.

The angle is \(300^{\circ}\), which is \(\frac{5}{3}\pi\) radians, approximately 5.23598775598299 radians, which is \(\frac{5}{6}\) of a turn, which is 0.833333333333333 turns.

Circle 3

  • The circle is cut into 4 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\omega\) (omega), subtends 1 of the sectors.

The angle is \(90^{\circ}\), which is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi\) radians, approximately 1.5707963267949 radians, which is \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a turn, which is 0.25 turns.

Circle 4

  • The circle is cut into 18 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\psi\) (psi), subtends 6 of the sectors.

The angle is \(120^{\circ}\), which is \(\frac{2}{3}\pi\) radians, approximately 2.0943951023932 radians, which is \(\frac{1}{3}\) of a turn, which is 0.333333333333333 turns.

Circle 5

  • The circle is cut into 20 congruent sectors. The central angle, \(\beta\) (beta), subtends 16 of the sectors.

The angle is \(288^{\circ}\), which is \(\frac{8}{5}\pi\) radians, approximately 5.02654824574367 radians, which is \(\frac{4}{5}\) of a turn, which is 0.8 turns.
